def reorder_by_permutation(items, perm):
    return [items[p] for p in perm]

def sort_by_custom_rank_map(items, rank_map):
    return sorted(items, key=lambda it: (0, rank_map[it]) if it in rank_map else (1, 0))

def sort_tasks_by_priority_name(tasks, priority):
    priority_rank = {p: i for i, p in enumerate(priority)}
    in_priority = [t for t in tasks if t in priority_rank]
    not_in_priority = [t for t in tasks if t not in priority_rank]
    in_priority_sorted = sorted(in_priority, key=lambda t: priority_rank[t])
    not_in_priority_sorted = sorted(not_in_priority)
    return in_priority_sorted + not_in_priority_sorted

note: For a value in front that has duplicate occurrences in items, only one occurrence is moved to the front (the rest stay in their original relative position among the remaining items); the spec and examples do not cover duplicates.

def reorder_by_priority_with_fallback_alpha(items, priority):
    priority_rank = {p: i for i, p in enumerate(priority)}
    in_priority = [it for it in items if it in priority_rank]
    not_in_priority = [it for it in items if it not in priority_rank]
    in_priority_sorted = sorted(in_priority, key=lambda it: priority_rank[it])
    not_in_priority_sorted = sorted(not_in_priority)
    return in_priority_sorted + not_in_priority_sorted

note: When every value is equal (min == max), the spec's "maximum value goes into the last bucket" rule would be ambiguous (every value is also the minimum); I put all values in bucket 0 in that case, consistent with the third example ([1,1,1], 3) which expects everything in the first bucket.
